text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[128,256],"block_K":[32,64,128],"num_stages":[1,2],"threads":[128,256],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16,32,64]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":2,"launches":0.5,"pipeline":1,"footprint":1},"rationale":"History: baseline 128x64x64 s1 t256 sw0=3560.55us; 32x256x32 s1 t256 sw64=3518.99us; 32x256x32 s1 t128 sw64=2504.88us; 64x128x32 s2 t256 sw64=3989.52us; 32x256x32 s1 t64 sw64=2891.16us; 32x256x32 s1 t128 sw32=2503.47us (BEST, 278.9MB DRAM, 3 blocks/SM); 32x256x32 s1 t256 sw32=3443.78us; 64x128x64 s1 t128 sw64=2715.84us (531.6MB DRAM, worse than best). Lessons: threads=128 decisively beats 64 and 256 at the winning wide-N tile (higher blocks/SM); swizzle=32 and 64 are effectively tied near-best so further swizzle-only rounds are low value; block_N=256 with small block_M=32 wins; attempt-08 raised block_K to 64/128 with t128 and regressed (2715.84us), confirming small block_K=32 with s1 is favorable for this wide-N tile. To escape re-selecting the excluded 32x256x32 family and test a genuinely new structural point, this plan forces exploration via block_N in {128,256} but with block_M span {32,64,128}, block_K span {32,64,128}, num_stages narrowed to {1,2} (deeper stages have repeatedly regressed or tied), threads {128,256} (128 measured winner, 256 retained only to re-confirm at a new tile), and full swizzle [0,4,8,16,32,64] to test smaller panels not yet measured. Excluded tuples will be skipped so HiGHS is pushed toward untested (block_M,block_K,swizzle) combinations with the wide-N preference. Weights: traffic=2 (DRAM reduction tracked latency strongly), launches=0.5 (4096^2 grid already saturates), pipeline=1 (stage benefit unproven and s2 regressed here), footprint=1 to keep the estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages,4*block_M*block_N) under the 32768 cap. Next hypothesis: does a different block_M (64/128) with block_K=32 and t128 plus a smaller swizzle (4/8/16) beat the 2503.47us best, or does the best remain anchored at block_M=32/block_N=256/block_K=32/s1/t128? If wide-N at small block_M still wins, drop block_N=128 and block_M=128 next round to concentrate on fine swizzle/block_K=32 variations at t128. Scope: Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR but do NOT execute the CUDA binary; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed."}
